explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/644 (EFKT92 proved f(k,3) = 2k). The statement f(k,r) ≤ 2k for r ≥ 3 is the elementary upper bound: two disjoint edges plus the 2-transversal condition on triples force e ∪ f to be a transversal. `subfamilyTransversalBound k r 2` is the least b such that every k-uniform family (possibly infinite, on any vertex type) whose ≤ r-element subfamilies have transversals of size ≤ 2 has a transversal of size ≤ b. That matches f(k,r). Proved in the file. Faithful.
